notes.title: About the Art and the Artist
notes.notes:
[p]Art is an aspect of the Four Divine Abidings that frequently receives compliments. It draws initial attention, supports a calm atmosphere, and communicates meaning for the game's Encounters. It is all [i]hand-painted[/i] in watercolor, which creates quite a unique look for a [i]digital[/i] product.[/p][p]I was very fortunate to meet Natali Arsenova through a friend's recommendation. She created all the hand-painted artwork for the game over the course of several months. Today we'd like to share her story.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611635/8cbfcc6d20040b1a4f4b66971c307f5bdf2c4a63.png"][/img][/p][p]"My name is Natasha Arsenova. I am 34 years old and live in Podgorica, Montenegro. I am a drawing teacher, a creative person, and I love to go hiking.[/p][p]I am an artist-painter-teacher by education. I studied for 5 years at college and 3 years as a book illustrator at an institute. I loved drawing so much that I could draw after classes and on weekends! I drew everywhere: at the station when waiting for the train, at friends' parties, on trips![/p][p]I was born in Siberia, Russia, and every summer we went to the Altai Mountains to draw in nature and hike in the mountains.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611635/750b187f5170a0b66ae6cdd6c5d70c8dd28a2898.png"][/img][/p][p]I worked as a 2D artist for 12 years, drawing for computer games. The most well-known game I worked on is Beholder, parts 1 and 2, for Steam. But in February, my life turned upside down. On February 9, 2022, my son died 43 days after birth - he had a heart defect and did not survive the operation. This was the most terrible period in my life and it changed me profoundly.[/p][p]I could not return to my previous job, so my husband and I moved to another country. Here, I began to try new things and get to know myself. I fell in love with watercolor, conducted master classes, and tried teaching. This whole journey led me to where I am now: teaching drawing in Podgorica and online. I am preparing for an exhibition in August and am happy that I am in my place, doing what I love."[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611635/86210bcaf647471d854f80f30902b47348a73dd5.png"][/img][/p][p]
[/p]

notes.title: Launch week recap and what's next
notes.notes: [h2]Launch week[/h2][p]For me as a developer of a free game, the key performance indicator (KPI) is player engagement and enjoyment with Four Divine Abidings. It tells me if it makes sense in further development or is it better to move on. For the first week, this KPI can be summarized in the following numbers:[/p][p][/p][p]⬖ 418 daily active players.[/p][p]⬖ 10h 5m median play time.[/p][p]⬖ 79 [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3834680/Four_Divine_Abidings_Supporter/"]Supporters[/url].[/p][p]⬖ 21, 90% positive [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3655580/Four_Divine_Abidings/#app_reviews_hash"]reviews[/url].[/p][p]⬖ Ongoing engagement:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611635/176eb3673dd65a8b2d15a1a6b6b6d3d5d41d6b54.png"][/img][/p][p]I'm thankful for the feedback and suggestions provided, which have already resulted in game updates improving the players' experience ([url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/3655580/view/670589610075619871?l=english"]1[/url], [url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/3655580/view/670589610075619520?l=english"]2[/url]). I'd like to specifically thank people who provided this feedback as well as those who wrote extensive reviews covering different aspects of the game, including the theme - I experienced appreciative joy reading them ([i]Mudita[/i] :) ).[/p][p]I've recently added [url="https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3527049699"]Beginner Insights[/url] which cover some of the early game basics to make first steps smoother.[/p][p][/p][h2]What's next[/h2][p]Given such engagement, I'm happy to continue the development, integrating the feedback and ideas that you provided. I've thematically grouped some of them:[/p][p]⬖ A glossary, where every term, whether game systems or lore related, can be easily searched for.[/p][p]⬖ A place where all uncovered game lore can be easily viewed again.[/p][p]⬖ Real meditation instructions with a timer.[/p][p]All of these fit well into a Library - an addition to the game I will focus on. It will take some time to develop, so I'll make sure to still implement smaller suggesstions and improvements while this bigger add-on is being developed.[/p][p]I'm also working on Mac support: while the build is ready, there are restrictions that Apple implemented for developers of the country I'm from. If you are enrolled in the Apple developer program and would like to assist in signing the game - kindly contact me in [url="https://discord.com/invite/CujAfXU3ZS"]Discord[/url].[/p][p][/p][h2]Thanks for playing ❤️[/h2][p][/p][p][/p]

notes.title: About Rebirth game system
notes.notes: [p][b]There are two types of players[/b] in the incremental genre: those who like rebirth/prestige mechanics and those who don’t.[/p][p][/p][p]Why don't players like it? The obvious answer is: [b]progress loss[/b] - this [b]is the actual thing the players don’t like.[/b][/p][p][/p][p]When crafting the Four Divine Abidings I pondered on this topic a lot to make Rebirths actually fun. These are game design solutions I implemented:[/p][p]⬖ Counter surface progress loss with more fundamental progress gain.[/p][p]⬖ Introduce resources that are consistent throughout the whole game and never lost.[/p][p]⬖ Add unique skills and systems accessible through Rebirths only.[/p][p]⬖ Make main game loop evolving and flexible.[/p][p]⬖ Introduce meaningful choices to customize each Rebirth.[/p][p]⬖ Add means of progress automation.[/p][p]⬖ Keep Rebirth system lore-consistent.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611635/069ea97e31e329f55696d9583f8c218ac87c6616.png"][/img][/p][p]On a design level it all might sound too abstract so here are some particulars that make Rebirths really fun in the Four Divine Abidings:[/p][p]⬖ [b]16 unique Rebirths skills[/b] grouped into 6 categories. Each category has an independent price curve so players can meaningfully choose what to focus on.[/p][p]⬖ [b]Free respecs[/b] always available for each Rebirth: trying new things is encouraged, makes runs different.[/p][p]⬖ [b]Rebirths preview[/b]: players see what stats they will have at the start, what buffs will be applied. Support theory craft and number crunching for those who like it.[/p][p]⬖ Main Rebirth resource - [b]Karma[/b] - [b]is never lost[/b], it accumulates through all runs. Besides, all Karma spent on Rebirths is converted to another resource - Merit - making the start of each run progressively more abundant. [/p][p]⬖ [b]Permanent buffs[/b] (that come from Milestones) are always preserved as well as Milestones themselves.[/p][p]⬖ An optional, upgradeable [b]tool that automates some progress[/b], especially effective early after Rebirths.[/p][p]⬖ [b]Rebirths fit the lore perfectly[/b] - it’s a central concept of the Buddhist philosophy which the lore itself is based on.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611635/9012e79bdf7aa7095df9ddce865d9c3d17b50162.png"][/img][/p][p]You are welcome to share your Rebirth system experience on Steam forums or [url="https://discord.com/invite/CujAfXU3ZS"][u]Discord[/u][/url].[/p]

notes.title: Active or idle?
notes.notes:
[p]When designing the Four Divine Abidings, one of my goals was to let players experience the game in the way they prefer. While starting mostly active, like many other games of the incremental genre, I aimed to gradually introduce idle play options that would be not much less efficient compared to active playstyle. [/p][p]Some notable features I integrated:[/p][p][/p][p]⬖ A tool which performs most manual actions for you, when unlocked and upgraded. At higher levels it even becomes more effective than clicking.[/p][p]⬖ A long offline time upgradeable up to 52 hours with fair calculations: exactly the same as the game was running.[/p][p]⬖ Idle rewards bonus that specifically applies when you don’t do most of the manual actions. And this bonus applies to offline time as well![/p][p]⬖ Click cooldowns: non-stop clicking is impossible. This allows to balance the game properly for any playstyle.[/p][p]⬖ Non-losable progress: the game always moves forward. There are no situations where a full game restart is a preferable option. No matter the players' choices, the progress happens, though with different pace.[/p][p][/p][p]Another design goal was to make active playstyle engaging. Since the game length is measured in weeks, pure clicking as the main mechanic can’t hold its place for that long. So I introduced features to keep players’ experience engaging throughout the whole game:
[/p][p]⬖ For the early game: 3 distinct mechanics for clicking: actual progress, energy restoration and stats boosts. A total of 9 clicking areas make the process more diverse. At the same time all of these mechanics are optional and it’s up to you when and how to engage.[/p][p]⬖ For the mid and late game: 202 milestones to complete and dozens of narrated tasks to follow. All of these activities favor mindful engagement, build customization and planning. This is the spot where players who like crunching numbers can engage the most. [/p][p]⬖ Several layers of intertwined game mechanics to experiment with. Through some months and many rounds of testing these are balanced to keep you trying different ones and feel rewarded most of the time. [/p][p]⬖ Evolving game loops. There is no single most effective setup for the whole game. At different stages, and for different tasks, some setups and play approaches are more effective than others.[/p][p]⬖ As support for the broken mouse convention: optional 2x game speed. If you really want, you can click A LOT :)) 
[/p][p]Summary: the game can be very idle and very active. One can turn it into a meditative experience with very little active engagement, or make active actions almost constantly, or a mix of both. It’s up to you to choose.[/p][p]
[/p]

notes.title: Blending Gaming and Mindfulness
notes.notes: [p][b]Some time ago I started with an idea[/b][/p][p]To create something different - an idle game that actually [i]helps you slow down[/i]. A mindfulness-themed game that lets you grow and progress while practicing real contemplative principles. The twist? You don't need to constantly click or grind. Progress happens naturally, reflecting the idea that sometimes the best action is knowing when not to act.[/p][p][b]Why?[/b][/p][p]Gaming helped me through some tough times, but I noticed something missing. While there are hundreds of games about fighting, building empires, or chasing high scores, almost none explore inner peace, mindfulness, or contemplative wisdom.[/p][p]After my own meditation and mindfulness practice changed my life, I realized I could create something unique - a game that's actually good for your mental health. A digital space where you can encounter timeless wisdom while having fun.[/p][p][b]How[/b][/p][p]The game design itself teaches mindfulness concepts:[/p][list][*][p][i]Automatic progress[/i] reflects letting go of constant striving[/p][/*][*][p][i]Cyclical gameplay[/i] mirrors the natural rhythms of life and meditation[/p][/*][*][p][i]Mindful choices[/i] over frantic clicking encourages presence[/p][/*][*][p][i]Visual meditation[/i] through carefully hand-crafted, calming aesthetics[/p][/*][/list][p]Every system is designed to embody contemplative principles rather than just reference them. You're not just reading about letting go - you're experiencing it through gameplay.[/p][p][b]Then I poured 3000 hours and my heart into implementation[/b][/p][p]And made this happen. At the same time I got a valuable opportunity to make the game free.[/p][p]I'm putting the finishing touches on this gaming experience. Follow along as I share development updates, mindful gaming philosophy, and sneak peeks at the meditative world I'm creating.[/p]
